answer_text:
Let

\[
f(z)=e^{z^{2}}.
\]

The integrand is

\[
\frac{e^{z^{2}}}{z-1}=\frac{f(z)}{z-1},
\]

which has a simple pole at \(z=1\). The rectangle \(\gamma\) has vertices

\[
(0,-1)\to(3,-1)\to(3,1)\to(0,1),
\]

so the point \(z=1\) lies strictly inside \(\gamma\). The function \(f(z)=e^{z^{2}}\) is entire, so it is analytic on and inside \(\gamma\).

Assuming the vertices are given in counterclockwise order, the contour is positively oriented. By Cauchy’s integral formula,

\[
\int_\gamma \frac{f(z)}{z-1}\,dz
=
2\pi i f(1).
\]

Since

\[
f(1)=e^{1^2}=e,
\]

we get

\[
\int_\gamma \frac{e^{z^{2}}}{z-1}\,dz
=
2\pi i e.
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{2\pi i e}
\]
